import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 419

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/419](https://www.erdosproblems.com/419)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [EGIP96] Erdős, Paul and Graham, S. W. and Ivić, Aleksandar and Pomerance, Carl,
  *On the number of divisors of $n!$*. (1996), 337--355.
-/

open Filter
open scoped ArithmeticFunction.sigma

namespace Erdos419

/-- The ratio $\sigma_0((n+1)!)/\sigma_0(n!)$, where $\sigma_0$ is the divisor-counting function. -/
noncomputable def factorialDivisorRatio (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  (σ 0 (n + 1).factorial : ℝ) / (σ 0 n.factorial : ℝ)

/-- The set $\{1\} \cup \{1+1/k : k \geq 1\}$. -/
def limitPointSet : Set ℝ :=
  {1} ∪ {x | ∃ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k ∧ x = 1 + 1 / (k : ℝ)}

/--
If $\tau(n)$ counts the number of divisors of $n$, then what is the set of limit points of
$$
\frac{\tau((n+1)!)}{\tau(n!)}?
$$

The limit points are exactly $\{1\} \cup \{1+1/k : k \geq 1\}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos419.lean"]
theorem erdos_419 :
    {x : ℝ | MapClusterPt x atTop factorialDivisorRatio} = limitPointSet := by
  sorry

end Erdos419

reformulations.difference: Lean uses MapClusterPt atTop for the sequence d((n+1)!)/d(n!) indexed from n = 0. EGIP96 Corollary 1 uses ordinary limit-point terminology and the shifted sequence d(n!)/d((n−1)!).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For real sequences, MapClusterPt x atTop is equivalent to convergence to x along a strictly increasing subsequence. Writing s(n) for the paper's ratio and r(n) for factorialDivisorRatio, s(n+1) = r(n). Since mapping atTop on ℕ by n ↦ n+1 gives atTop again, the cluster-point sets coincide. Both the subsequence equivalence and the index-shift equivalence were proved without sorry in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

sources_consulted: Erdős and Graham, Old and New Problems and Results in Combinatorial Number Theory (1980), p. 83 (PDF page 79): https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~ronspubs/80_11_number_theory.pdf
Erdős, S. W. Graham, Ivić and Pomerance, On the Number of Divisors of n! (1996), §3, Theorem 2 and Corollary 1 (PDF pp. 4–5): https://math.dartmouth.edu/~carlp/factorial.pdf
Erdős bibliography, including the 1980 book entry: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/Erdos.html
